summary: Global equities had their worst week in over 18 months as AI-spending doubts, a reported SEC probe of Nvidia and a possible NAND oversupply hit chips: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Friday to 6,910 (-8.6% on the week) and the VIX rose to about 36, while the Nikkei and Kospi each fell more than 5%. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.92% even as Fed governor Waller argued for a half-point December hike, and Bank Indonesia raised its rate to 6.00% to defend the rupiah. Resource markets sold off too: copper hit its lowest since April (-9.9% on the week), gold fell about 9% and silver about 16%, Brent and WTI slipped on a US crude build despite Hormuz tanker attacks, and EU gas storage sat at a record low for the date.
